title: Libra: A Hybrid-Sparse Attention Accelerator Featuring Multi-Level Workload Balance
problem: Transformer inference is bottlenecked by high computational complexity and memory usage; hybrid sparsity (value-level + bit-level) can improve efficiency but causes severe load imbalance across compute units, limiting actual acceleration benefits.
motivation: Transformers are pervasive in NLP, but inference efficiency is critical for deployment; higher sparsity provides acceleration potential, but load imbalance undermines utilization when both value and bit sparsity are exploited.
method: Libra uses filtered bit-group sparsification (removing groups of zero bits from weights) and dynamic bit-group quantization (reducing activation bit-width), which creates irregular computation demands across compute units. The hardware addresses this with a task pool and multi-level workload balancing to keep all units equally busy, plus an adaptive bit-width architecture that lets different parts compute at different precisions simultaneously.
key_novelty: It's the first attention accelerator combining weight and bit-level sparsity that solves the load-imbalance problem through multi-level task scheduling and variable bit-width execution.
contributions: Filtered bit-group sparsification (FBS) for structured weight sparsity
Dynamic bit-group quantization (DBQ) for activation-level sparsification
Multi-level task pool for workload balancing across compute units
Adaptive bit-width architecture enabling parallel execution at varying bit-widths
1.49-5.89x speedup vs. SOTA, 2.65-10.82x energy efficiency improvement
